pilotMechanism.statute: Long Term Tax Exemption Law (N.J.S.A. 40A:20-1 et seq.)
pilotMechanism.pilotExplanation: Under New Jersey PILOT laws, developers pay an annual service charge directly to Hawthorne Borough municipal government instead of regular property taxes. The public school district receives 0%, shifting the school operational cost onto residential homeowners.

taxpayerSolutions.title: Mandate Statutory PILOT School Sharing
taxpayerSolutions.mechanism: Amend N.J.S.A. 40A:20-12 to require municipal governments to share PILOT revenue with school boards proportional to school levy share.
taxpayerSolutions.taxpayerBenefit: Would restore approximately $40k directly to Hawthorne Borough school taxes.

taxpayerSolutions.title: Perform Strict Annual Commercial Revaluations
taxpayerSolutions.mechanism: Annual assessment maintenance prevents abrupt commercial tax appeal refund deficits.
taxpayerSolutions.taxpayerBenefit: Eliminates sudden municipal debt issuance for commercial tax refund settlements.

taxpayerSolutions.title: Enforce Transparent Financial Disclosure on Developer PILOTs
taxpayerSolutions.mechanism: Require developers to post audited financial statements on municipal portal prior to tax abatement renewals.
taxpayerSolutions.taxpayerBenefit: Guarantees public oversight of developer returns and statutory excess profit returns.

taxpayerSolutions.title: Regional Shared Municipal Infrastructure
taxpayerSolutions.mechanism: Join Passaic County shared service compacts for DPW heavy equipment, paving, and joint dispatch.
taxpayerSolutions.taxpayerBenefit: Trims 1.5% to 3.0% off the local municipal operating tax levy.
